comment: The vectors pinning Prima.LocusBackends, the backends wire between CYFR's controller and the backends service Locus serves; apps/prima/test/prima/locus_backends_test.exs consumes every section, and every end of the wire (the Locus service, CYFR's client and the image probe) reproduces them. Every consumer derives the control, seal and owner keys from the service key over the label, reproduces each control message's and the invoke's canonical string, MAC and header, reads each control body and its answer to its members and writes them back to the same bytes, opens the sealed environment for its owner and lifetime only, parses every accepted header and refuses every malformed one as its kind, refuses every invalid message with the error named and answers it with the refusal named, refuses every header under auth_rejected at its instant with its reason, and masks the input to the output. Integers are decimal in canonical strings and headers, and a header names its body's hex SHA-256 as body=, which an accepted header parses to as its body_hash. reserved_env_prefixes is written as it is once the MCP bridge is retired, LOCUS_ in place of MCP_BRIDGE_; until then Prima.KeeperProtocol's list, which the wire reserves, still names MCP_BRIDGE_. The fences (stale_boot, stale_control, stale_epoch, epoch_ahead, replay) are the service's and are named under refusals only.
